correctness.rationale: For every labelled vertex permutation of the fourteen-vertex Fano Levi graph, the prefix-cut identity and the rigorously derived minimum cut profile give a cost lower bound of 69. The paired disjoint six-cycle construction reaches equality, and equality forces exactly those endpoint cycles, their internal arc orders, and the two middle vertices. There are 28 first cycles, three disjoint mates, 96 arc orders each, and two middle orders, giving exactly 1,548,288 distinct optimum permutations. Two independently represented finite verifiers exhaust all 16,384 vertex subsets, independently count all optimal chains, enumerate all disjoint cycle pairs, and agree on the result.

originality.rationale: The claim classifies and counts all Heawood minimum linear arrangements. The classical general minimum-cut/arrangement equivalence does not fix the Heawood profile or enumerate its nested optimal chains. The previously known 28 six-cycles and their cubic disjointness graph do not imply that precisely these paired hexagons and arc orders characterize every optimum. value.rationale: For a canonical fourteen-vertex incidence graph, the theorem completely enumerates optimal linear layouts instead of merely reporting one optimum. It connects the natural minimum edge-isoperimetric profile to the classical Coxeter graph on Heawood six-cycles, yields all attaining permutations without testing 14! orders, and supplies an exact benchmark for constrained-cut and optimal-layout enumeration. This complete optimizer classification is intrinsically motivated by the graph and the layout problem, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
